My name na Mark Holland. Two winter wey don pass, I learn the difference between to strong and to dey saved.
For nineteen years, I dey run lathe for the same shop near Saginaw. I sabi the work well. I fit fix anything.
Then one Friday for November, dem lock the gate with chain. No warning. Na only paper for the fence, and last check.
I tell my wife Jenna make she no worry. I talk am like man wey get plan.
I no get plan. Wetin I get na CV wey nobody call back, truck payment, mortgage, and two pikin wey still believe say their papa fit do anything.
I do everything wey dem say make person do. I apply for forty-one work. I drive go job fair. I sell my tools, one by one.
And every week, the pile for table dey high pass before. And something inside me dey quiet more and more.
For February, dem come carry the truck. Lily, she be nine years, stand for front window with her socks, dey watch as dem hook am.
She no cry. She just look me. I think say that one worse pass.
Na there hopeless turn to helpless.
Hopeless na when you no fit see road comot. Helpless na when you no believe again say your own hand fit make road.
I go dey sit for garage after everybody don sleep. I no dey do anything. Just dey sit. I no want make anybody see me like that.
Mark, talk to me. Call somebody. Call your brother. Call Pastor Dave. Pray with me.
And I talk the thing wey I no proud of. I say, Pray? Jenna, prayer no dey pay mortgage. I need do something.
I no know say Owen dey for staircase. Him be fourteen.
Him come down the next morning as I dey look my coffee, and him ask me question wey I no fit answer.
Him say, Daddy, for youth group dem dey tell us, when you no get anybody else to call, call Jesus.
But no be wetin people dey talk when dem don give up? Like, if you no fit fix am, you go pray?
I wan tell am yes. Na wetin I believe be that. Prayer na for when real work don finish.
To reach for your phone na for scrolling, no be for help. Man no dey reach out. Man dey figure am out.
But that night, for three o'clock for morning, nothing remain for me to take figure am out.
Jenna don put one app for my phone weeks before. Community Covenant. I never open am. I tell myself say I go just look. I press play.
I go lift my eye look the hills, where my help go come from. My help dey come from the Lord, wey make heaven and earth. Psalm one twenty one.
My help dey come. No be, my help go come after I don do enough.
Then the reel talk something wey I never forget. When Peter dey sink for water, him no swim first. Him no make plan.
Him shout, Lord, save me. And sharp sharp Jesus stretch Him hand, catch am. Matthew fourteen, thirty and thirty one.
To cry out no be to give up. To cry out na the first correct thing wey Peter do.
So I do the one thing wey I fit do. I open the box wey say, How you dey? And for the first time for four months, I talk the truth.
I type, I no dey okay. I lose my work. I lose my truck. I no know who I be if I no fit provide. I no get anybody else to call.
I sleep off for there. When I wake, reply dey wait me. Real one. Somebody read every word.
Mark, you no dey alone, and God no mean make you carry this one by yourself. Romans ten thirteen talk say, anybody wey call the name of the Lord go dey saved.
To call no be the end of your work. Na the beginning.
Na wetin I finally tell Owen be that. My son, to call Jesus no be wetin you do instead of to do something. Na the first something.
Faith dey come first. Bible talk say, without faith, e no possible to please Him. Hebrews eleven, six.
Noah no build the ark before him believe. Him believe God. Then him carry the hammer.
And faith wey no dey carry hammer no be real faith. James talk am plain.
Faith wey no get work, e don die, as e dey alone. James two, seventeen.
So the order matter. Faith first, then the work. The root, then the fruit.
So every morning after that, before I open laptop, me and Jenna put our hand for the applications and pray Proverbs sixteen, three.
Commit your work give the Lord, and your thoughts go stand well.
I don dey try make my own thoughts stand for months. Dem dey scatter. So I start to commit the work first.
Nothing change overnight. I no go tell you say check show for mailbox. Wetin change na me.
I take part-time work for hardware store for town. Eleven dollars for one hour. The old me for too proud.
The new me say, Lord, establish the work of my hand. Even this work. Psalm ninety, seventeen.
I start to dey fix things again. One widow for our road get furnace wey no gree light. I fix am free.
One man for church need make dem rebuild him porch. Me and Owen do am together, every Saturday.
I no dey wait make God move again. I dey move with Him.
And I continue to dey write for the app. Some days na just thank you. Some days na, still nothing. And somebody always reply.
One morning, one member wey I never meet read my log, write say her brother-in-law dey run factory two hours south. Dem dey find machinist.
I dey start every shift for there now. E take nine months from the day dem chain the gate. Nine months of faith and work, dey waka side by side.
Two better pass one, na so Bible talk. Because if dem fall, one go lift him companion up. Ecclesiastes four.
So why we dey tell you make you call Jesus when you no get anybody else to call? Because when you no get anybody, Him still dey there.
And because to call no be to quit. To reach for your phone for three o'clock for morning to talk say, I no dey okay. That one no be weakness.
Na the bravest work wey dey. Na the first work. Everything else go build on top am.
Lily ask me last week if I fear that time. I tell am the truth. Yes.
But to fear and to dey alone na two different things. I fear. I never dey alone. And you sef no dey alone.
If you dey inside your own winter now, no wait until you fix am before you reach out. Call Him first. Then carry the hammer.
Community Covenant. Press play. Talk the truth. Somebody go write back.
